title: Two localization triangles for gluing a generic retract
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, and a finite normed extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Put $A_{E,T}=p_T^*C(-,E)$ and $A_{\mathcal O_E,T}=p_T^*C(-,\mathcal O_E)$, with continuous-map condensed rings and their norm topologies [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Write $\Dbc(T,A_E)$ for bounded complexes with finite constant local models on finite constructible stratifications [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Lisse means pro-etale locally finite free, including rank zero [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module].

A full thick subcategory means a full subcategory containing zero and closed under isomorphisms, shifts, finite sums, distinguished-triangle cones and retracts [def-weil-triangulated-category]; a retract is a pair of maps whose composite on the smaller object is its identity. Let $a:S\hookrightarrow U$ be a locally closed immersion with $S$ nonempty integral and $Z=\overline S\subseteq U$. Let $v:S_0\hookrightarrow S$ be a nonempty dense open immersion and $z:B=(S\setminus S_0)_{\rm red}\hookrightarrow S$ its closed complement. Put $F=\overline B\subseteq U$. Then $F$ is a proper closed subset of $Z$. Let $M,N\in\Dbc(S,A_E)$, and suppose maps
$$v^*M\xrightarrow{\iota}v^*N\xrightarrow{\rho}v^*M,\qquad\rho\iota=1_{v^*M}$$
are given in $D(S_0,A_E)$. All locally closed extensions have the exact normalized meaning of [lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence]. There are distinguished triangles in $D(U,A_E)$
$$ (av)_!v^*N\longrightarrow a_!N\longrightarrow a_!z_*z^*N\longrightarrow ((av)_!v^*N)[1],$$
$$ (av)_!v^*M\longrightarrow a_!M\longrightarrow a_!z_*z^*M\longrightarrow ((av)_!v^*M)[1].$$
Both third terms belong to $\Dbc(U,A_E)$ and restrict to zero on $U\setminus F$. The maps $(av)_!\iota,(av)_!\rho$ exhibit $(av)_!v^*M$ as a retract of $(av)_!v^*N$. Consequently, if a full thick subcategory $\mathcal H\subseteq D(U,A_E)$ contains $a_!N$ and every bounded constructible complex supported on $F$, then it contains $(av)_!v^*N$, $(av)_!v^*M$ and $a_!M$. If $S_0=S$, the error terms are zero. This conclusion uses only the two displayed triangles and the displayed retract, without extending the projector to $a_!N$.

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0,k$), so every scheme in the statement is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-complementary-stratifications] to each open/closed pair below: all its schemes are qcqs and its open immersion is quasi-compact. Topologically, a locally closed subset $S$ is open in its closure $Z$: if $S=V\cap C$ with $V$ open and $C$ closed in $U$, then $Z\subseteq C$ and $Z\cap V=S$. Thus $S_0$ is a nonempty open subset of $Z$. The closed subset $Z\setminus S_0$ of $U$ contains $B$, hence contains $F=\overline B$. Consequently $F\subsetneq Z$.

proof.text: Use $\Lambda=C(-,E)$. The Cartesian coefficient isomorphisms and exact pullback of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identify all inverse-image rings with the specified $A_{E,T}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] to $(v,z)$ on $S$. By [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport], its exact functors, specified units/counits and short exact sequence transport to internal modules. For every internal module $L$ we obtain $0\to v_!v^*L\to L\to z_*z^*L\to0$. The same inputs apply to any other complementary pair used below; in particular closed direct image restricts to zero on the complementary open. The quasi-compactness hypothesis is supplied by step 1.

proof.text: For $K=N$ and $K=M$, choose a complex representing $K$. The natural sequence of step 2 is degreewise short exact and hence a sequence of complexes. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] it gives the distinguished triangle $v_!v^*K\to K\to z_*z^*K\to(v_!v^*K)[1]$. The functor $a_!$ is exact by [lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence]; its termwise derived functor is triangulated by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Apply it to this triangle. The normalized composition isomorphism $a_!v_!\cong(av)_!$ from the coherence node identifies the first and shifted terms, giving exactly the two triangles asserted in the item.

proof.text: For $K=M,N$, [lem-sfb-pullback-constant-model-constructible] makes every $z^*H^q(K)$ constructible in the finite constant scalar-model sense. By [lem-sfb-scalar-model-immersion-extension], $z_*$ preserves those models. Factor $a$ as closed followed by open and apply that same node to the two extension factors; [lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence] identifies their composite with $a_!$. All these functors are exact, so they preserve kernels, images and their quotients, giving $H^q(a_!z_*z^*K)\cong a_!z_*z^*H^q(K)$. This vanishes outside the finite cohomological interval for $K$ and is constructible within it. Thus both third terms belong to $\Dbc(U,A_E)$ as defined in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. A finite $E$ can be embedded in an algebraic closure for the admissible-coefficient lemmas; their coefficient is the continuous condensed ring of that same finite field.

proof.text: Put $t=az:B\hookrightarrow U$. Composition coherence gives $a_!z_*\cong t_!$, using the closed comparison $z_!=z_*$. Since $B$ is reduced, [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-image] identifies the scheme-theoretic image of $t$ with the reduced closed scheme on $F$. The canonical immersion factorization in [def-sfb-locally-closed-coefficient-extension] is therefore $t=i_F b$, with $b:B\hookrightarrow F$ open and $i_F:F\hookrightarrow U$ closed; the normalized coherence node identifies $t_!\cong i_{F,*}b_!$. For the complementary open $w:U\setminus F\hookrightarrow U$, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] and [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport] give $w^*i_{F,*}=0$. Termwise this proves $w^*(a_!z_*z^*K)=0$ for $K=M,N$. This uses the scheme-theoretic image theorem, not just set-theoretic containment to assert a factorization.

proof.text: Functoriality gives $((av)_!\rho)\circ((av)_!\iota)=(av)_!(\rho\iota)=1$, the claimed retract. Write $C_K=a_!z_*z^*K$. Steps 4 and 5 put $C_M,C_N$ in $\mathcal H$. Rotate the $N$ triangle backwards, using TR2 of [def-weil-triangulated-category], to $C_N[-1]\to(av)_!v^*N\to a_!N\to C_N$. Equivalently $(av)_!v^*N$ is the cone, shifted by $-1$, of $a_!N\to C_N$; cone and shift closure put it in $\mathcal H$. Retract closure puts $(av)_!v^*M$ there. Rotating the $M$ triangle backwards shows $a_!M$ is the cone of $C_M[-1]\to(av)_!v^*M$, so it also belongs to $\mathcal H$. If $S_0=S$, then $B=\varnothing$: the empty covering forces every module on its site to be zero, so both $z^*K$ and both error terms are zero. These constructions use only the given maps on $S_0$.

F ⊊ Z holds because S is open in Z, so S0 is open in Z and F ⊆ Z∖S0. Step 2: Cartesian coefficients, ringed-open-closed (SES, j⁻¹i_*=0) and internal-module transport give the localization sequence for internal modules. Step 3: complex-SES triangle, the exact termwise a_! (coherence node plus exact-functor-derived-factorization) and γ_{a,v} give both triangles. Step 4: pullback-constant-model and scalar-model-immersion-extension, applied to z_* and to both factors of a, put the error terms in Dbc(U,A_E). The finite E embeds isometrically in Q̄_ℓ, so its condensed ring is the same C(−,E). Step 5: B is reduced, so the scheme-theoretic image of t is F_red; the canonical factorization t = i_F∘b and coherence give t_! ≅ i_{F*}b_!, and w*i_{F*} = 0. Step 6 is elementary: the retract by functoriality, then TR2 rotation with cone, shift and retract closure. I tested S0=S, M=0, N=0, dim 0, and U=A¹ with S0=A¹∖{0}; all are consistent.
